Everything so far, in the order you'd do it on the X32 before a show.

## The order on the X32

The X32 manual's own steps for a microphone on a channel:

1. Plug in; mute the channel and switch **48 V** on if it's a condenser.
2. **Gain**, using the input meter (loudest part around −12 to −6).
3. **Low Cut**, to remove rumble or wind.
4. **EQ**.
5. **Gate** and **Compressor**.
6. **Stereo Bus** on, and **Pan**.
7. The channel **fader** to around 0 dB, then slowly bring up the **Main LR** fader.

Then the monitor sends ([Live Sound 6](live-feedback.qmd)), one channel at a time, and finally the whole band
together, listened to from where the audience will be.

<div class="sk-tip">When it's right, <b>save a scene</b> (Scenes, View, Save). Next week you can recall it and
start from there instead of from zero.</div>

## Mystery channel

Each problem is one of these channels with one thing wrong. Listen, look at the meters, and say what it needs
first. Then fix it and press **Check my channel**.

<div class="lk" data-w="strip" data-quiz></div>

## Practice on the real X32

Every channel in these lessons can be played through the real desk. On a channel above, choose a source and
press **⤓ WAV**: 32 seconds of that sound, raw, with the problem still in it.

| File | What's wrong | Lesson |
|---|---|---|
| Podium speech | quiet talker: needs a lot of gain | [2](live-gain.qmd) |
| Boomy vocal | rumble, thumps, boom | [3](live-eq.qmd) |
| Harsh guitar | 3 kHz peak, fizz | [3](live-eq.qmd) |
| Kick drum mic | snare, hat and crash bleed | [4](live-gate.qmd) |
| Rack tom mic | ring and bleed | [4](live-gate.qmd) |
| Lead vocal | soft verse, loud chorus | [5](live-comp.qmd) |
| Bass DI | popped notes | [5](live-comp.qmd) |

<div class="lk" data-w="strip" data-source="kick" data-show="pre" data-title="Download a practice file"></div>

How to get them into a channel with the full strip:

- **From a laptop or phone**: its headphone output into a **DI box**, and the DI into any input 1–32. The DI
  turns it into a mic-level signal, so you set the Gain just like a mic.
- **Over USB** (if the desk has the X-USB card): play the file from the computer and patch the card's returns
  to input channels on the Routing screen.
- The X32's **USB stick player** comes back on the **Aux 7/8** channels. Aux In channels have EQ but no
  gate or compressor, so it's fine for the EQ files and not for the gate and compressor ones.

The files peak at −12 dBFS. Start with the gain low, the fader down, and work through the strip.
